{{alias}}( order, uplo, N, KD, AB, LDAB )
    Computes an unblocked Cholesky factorization of a real symmetric
    positive definite band matrix in place.

    H=KD+1; full compact AB is H-by-N. For zero-based i,j, upper input
    A(i,j) occupies band row KD+i-j; lower input occupies row i-j.
    KD may exceed N-1. Unused stars, padding and guards remain unchanged.
    Returns scalar INFO=0, or the first one-based failed diagonal for
    the source comparison AJJ<=0. The failed diagonal is not assigned
    at that step; previous factor and trailing updates remain. Later
    steps do not run. No rollback, PIV, RANK, WORK or TOL is provided.

    No added NaN/finite precheck is performed. INFO=0 does not certify
    finite factors or numerical stability. Even finite inputs can
    overflow a scaled coupling's rank update and return positive INFO.

    Positive N requires an intrinsic Float64Array with ordinary
    ArrayBuffer backing; current valid resizable extents are supported.
    SharedArrayBuffer is rejected. Backing must remain stable and
    exclusive until return: no resize, detach, transfer, reentry or
    concurrent foreign mutation. Hidden foreign physical aliases are
    outside the caller contract. Shadow properties do not override
    intrinsic metadata. The full band view must fit and be injective.

    For N=0, validate selectors, N, KD and main LDAB, then return zero
    without array/unused ndarray metadata access, dispatch or writes.
    Column-major LDAB>=H and row-major LDAB>=max(1,N) still apply.
    Scalar/geometry/helper eligibility selects native or JS before
    dispatch; unused singleton strides normalize after validation.
    Raw native/C integer domains differ from the public empty domain.

    TypeError rejects invalid selectors, active brands and backing.
    RangeError rejects integer, bounds or exact geometry violations
    before writes. Proposed engine metadata does not establish older
    Node/native compatibility; actual execution used Node24.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string|number
        Row-major (101) or column-major (102) compact-band layout.

    uplo: string|number
        Upper (121) or lower (122) stored triangle.

    N: integer
        Nonnegative safe matrix order, at most 2147483647.

    KD: integer
        Nonnegative safe bandwidth, at most 2147483647.

    AB: Float64Array
        Full input/output (KD+1)-by-N compact band view.

    LDAB: integer
        At least KD+1 column-major or max(1,N) row-major.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero or the first one-based failed diagonal.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 4, 10, 17, 2, 3, 999 ] );
    > {{alias}}( 'row-major', 'lower', 3, 1, A, 3 )
    0
    > A
    <Float64Array>[ 2, 3, 4, 1, 1, 999 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( uplo, N, KD, AB, r, c, o )
    Factors using signed independent element strides and an offset
    relative to the intrinsic typed-array view. Band row b/column j
    occupies AB[o+b*r+j*c]. Positive N validates the full H-by-N view,
    including unused stars. Used zero strides, colliding cells and
    unsafe endpoint arithmetic are rejected before writes.
    Empty calls do not inspect unused AB, r, c or o. The status,
    failure-prefix and backing/lifetime rules above apply.

    Parameters
    ----------
    uplo: string|number
        Upper (121) or lower (122) stored triangle.

    N: integer
        Nonnegative safe matrix order, at most 2147483647.

    KD: integer
        Nonnegative safe bandwidth, at most 2147483647.

    AB: Float64Array
        Full input/output (KD+1)-by-N compact band view.

    r: integer
        Band-row element stride.

    c: integer
        Matrix-column element stride.

    o: integer
        Starting compact band index.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero or the first one-based failed diagonal.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 7, 16, 0, 4, 7 ] );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'lower', 3, 0, A, 1, -1, 3 )
    2
    > A
    <Float64Array>[ 7, 16, 0, 2, 7 ]

    See Also
    --------
